summary: USCIS Alert: Key Updates on USCIS Operations (September 03, 2026)
details: Recent USCIS announcements highlight significant operational changes, including the opening of new international and asylum offices, updates to critical immigration forms, and new policies aimed at enhancing fraud prevention and electronic filing. These changes reflect USCIS's ongoing efforts to streamline processes and improve service delivery for applicants and practitioners alike.

alerts.summary: USCIS is launching a new international field office in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, starting September 9, 2026. This office aims to enhance the agency's ability to handle immigration matters in the region and strengthen fraud prevention efforts. The establishment of this office is crucial for applicants in Ethiopia, as it provides localized support and resources for navigating the immigration process.

alerts.summary: A recent order from the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California has placed a hold on specific USCIS policies, PM 602-0192 and PM 602-0194. This ruling may impact how certain immigration applications are processed, potentially delaying decisions for applicants affected by these policies. Practitioners should stay informed about the implications of this order as it may alter the landscape of immigration law and policy.
alerts.title: Recent Court Order on Hold Policies

alerts.summary: USCIS will release a revised edition of Form I-485 on September 18, 2026, after which older versions will be rejected. This update is essential for applicants seeking to adjust their status, as using outdated forms could lead to application delays or denials. Practitioners must ensure that their clients are aware of this change to avoid complications in their applications.

alerts.summary: USCIS has issued updated guidance regarding the public charge inadmissibility determination for applicants seeking adjustment of status. This guidance clarifies the criteria used to assess whether an applicant is likely to become a public charge, which is critical for individuals applying for permanent residency. Understanding these criteria is vital for applicants and practitioners to prepare strong applications that meet USCIS standards.
alerts.title: USCIS Issues Guidance on Making Public Charge Inadmissibility Determination

alerts.summary: On September 15, 2026, USCIS will publish revised editions of Form I-539 and Form I-765, with older versions being rejected thereafter. These forms are crucial for nonimmigrant status extensions and employment authorization, respectively. Applicants must use the updated forms to ensure their requests are processed without delays, making it essential for practitioners to inform their clients of this change.
alerts.title: USCIS to Publish New Editions of Form I-539 and Form I-765; Older Editions Will Be Rejected Starting Sept. 15

alerts.summary: DHS has introduced an interim final rule mandating electronic filing for certain immigration forms. This move aims to enhance national security and streamline processing times. alerts.summary: USCIS is clarifying that applicants must establish eligibility for immigration benefits at the time of filing. This policy aims to reduce frivolous requests and ensure that only valid applications are submitted. These actions signal a robust enforcement approach by USCIS and the Department of Justice, emphasizing the importance of integrity in the immigration process and the consequences of fraudulent activities.
